text_read: reader extract of the dlshq.org book page (introduction); chapters not read
mode_evidence: The deity image is 'visualised' after alternating open-eye gazing and eye closure; nothing says it becomes perceived. Coloured lights are mentioned only as something to ignore.
onset_evidence: No claim that japa produces seen light. For someone who cannot visualise: picture any part, or a hazy image, and let it sharpen; failing that, fix the mind on the effulgent light in the heart. Time scale: 'some months' for a clear image.

conditions.gaze_or_eye_position: Open-eye gaze at picture, then closed eyes
conditions.duration_and_schedule: A few minutes of gazing; 5-6 alternations; months

what_to_do_with_light: Ignore visions and coloured lights; treat the heart-light as the form of the Ishta if the image will not come.
obstacles_and_fixes: Cannot hold full image: visualise a part or a hazy image
Still failing: fix the mind on the light in the heart
cautions: Ignore the visions and coloured lights
interpretation: Lights and visions are by-products to be disregarded; the heart-light can stand in for the deity's form.
practice_summary: Gaze at a picture of your Ishta-Devata for a few minutes, close the eyes and try to hold it; when it fades open the eyes and gaze again; repeat five or six times, for months, until the image is clear. If the whole image will not come, take a part or a hazy outline; if that fails, rest the mind on the effulgent light in the heart and treat it as the deity. In silent early-morning meditation, sit motionless and ignore any visions or coloured lights.

key_passages.anchor: Gaze at the picture of the Lord, your Ishta-Devata, for a few minutes, and close your eyes.
key_passages.paraphrase: Alternate open-eye gazing at the picture with closed-eye holding, 5-6 times.

key_passages.anchor: fix the mind on the effulgent light in the heart
Sit motionless and calm in the early morning hours. Ignore the visions and coloured lights.
